result.title: DiTraR: Diverse Scorers and Transcript-Guided Re-ranking for Video Corpus Moment Retrieval
result.summary: Video corpus moment retrieval asks a system to find, in a large collection of untrimmed videos with subtitles, the video and the time interval that a natural-language query describes. We find that most top-ranked errors of a strong corpus-level scorer come from choosing the wrong video, not from imprecise boundaries, and that re-weighting the evidence the scorer already uses does not fix them. We present DiTraR, which addresses video selection from two complementary directions. A witness-interval scorer decomposes the query into probes and scores every candidate interval of every corpus video exactly; a multi-scorer energy ensemble averages the energies of independently trained scorers before one exhaustive search; and a transcript verifier, a frozen language model that reads the time-stamped dialogue of the highest-ranked videos, re-orders the moments without changing their boundaries. With all settings frozen on development data and a single evaluation, DiTraR reaches 24.36 and 13.55 R@1 at IoU 0.5 and 0.7 on the TVR validation split. The ensemble improves queries about visual content, the verifier improves queries about dialogue, and their gains largely add up.

AI.brief_summary: 论文分析视频语料时刻检索中主要错误来自「选错视频」而非边界不准，提出 DiTraR：将查询拆成探针并穷举评分候选区间的 witness-interval 评分器、多评分器能量集成，以及用冻结语言模型读取高排名视频的时间戳对白来重排但不改边界的 transcript 验证器。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把片段定位与证据核验显式解耦，并以集成评分和文本验证器分别改善视觉类与对白类查询，可能可供核查 LVR 中多假设评分、模态特异性证据筛选以及「先定位后核验」分工的借鉴线索；但论文本身不涉及 latent 推理状态。
